ingredientsJSON.value: [{"item":"tomatoes","section":"For the tomato juice","qty":"500","unit":"g","notes":"cut into large pieces"},{"item":"tamarind","section":"For the tomato juice","qty":"20","unit":"g","notes":"about lemon-sized"},{"item":"water","section":"For the tomato juice","qty":"4","unit":"cups","notes":"about 1 liter"},{"item":"toor dal","section":"For the rasam powder","qty":"1","unit":"tbsp"},{"item":"coriander seeds","section":"For the rasam powder","qty":"1","unit":"tsp"},{"item":"cumin seeds","section":"For the rasam powder","qty":"1/2","unit":"tsp"},{"item":"fenugreek seeds","section":"For the rasam powder","qty":"1/4","unit":"tsp"},{"item":"dried red chilies","section":"For the rasam powder","qty":"3-4"},{"item":"black pepper","section":"For the rasam powder","qty":"1","unit":"tsp"},{"item":"garlic cloves","section":"For the rasam powder","qty":"5-6","notes":"added last, blended coarsely into the powder"},{"item":"turmeric powder","section":"For the rasam","qty":"1/2","unit":"tsp"},{"item":"salt","section":"For the rasam","notes":"to taste"},{"item":"fresh coriander","section":"For the rasam","qty":"a little","notes":"crushed by hand"},{"item":"curry leaves","section":"For the rasam","qty":"a bit","notes":"crushed"},{"item":"green chilies","section":"For the rasam","qty":"2","notes":"slit"},{"item":"oil","section":"For tempering","qty":"1","unit":"tbsp"},{"item":"chana dal","section":"For tempering"},{"item":"urad dal","section":"For tempering"},{"item":"mustard seeds","section":"For tempering"},{"item":"cumin seeds","section":"For tempering"},{"item":"dried red chilies","section":"For tempering"},{"item":"garlic cloves","section":"For tempering","qty":"a few","notes":"chopped"},{"item":"curry leaves","section":"For tempering","qty":"a bit"},{"item":"fresh coriander","section":"For tempering","qty":"some","notes":"finely chopped, to finish"}]

stepsJSON.value: [{"text":"Add the tamarind and tomatoes (cut into large pieces) into a mixer jar. Grind coarsely — not into a smooth paste or puree, just broken down roughly."},{"text":"Place a strainer over a large bowl. Pour in the ground mixture and gradually add about 4 cups (1 liter) of water, squeezing or pressing with a hand or ladle, to extract all the juice and separate the peels, seeds, and pulp completely. Set the strained tomato juice aside."},{"text":"Heat a dry pan on low heat. Add toor dal, coriander seeds, cumin, fenugreek, dried red chilies, and pepper. Dry roast slowly until just slightly warm and golden — do not let the color darken too much. Remove from heat and let cool completely."},{"text":"Grind the cooled roasted ingredients into a smooth powder in a mixer. Add 5–6 garlic cloves and blend again coarsely. This is the rasam powder; set it aside."},{"text":"Pour the strained tomato juice into a pot. Add turmeric, salt to taste, crushed fresh coriander, crushed curry leaves, slit green chilies, and all the prepared rasam powder. Mix well and adjust salt."},{"text":"Place the pot on medium flame and simmer until the rasam reduces slightly, about 10–15 minutes.","durationSec":750},{"text":"Make the tempering: heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a small pan. Add chana dal, urad dal, mustard seeds, cumin, and dried chilies; sauté briefly until they splutter. Add chopped garlic and curry leaves, sauté once, then turn off the heat."},{"text":"Pour the tempering into the simmered rasam. Add finely chopped fresh coriander, mix well, and serve hot with plain steamed rice and papads."}]

summary.value: A tangy, spicy South Indian soup made with fresh tomatoes and tamarind, flavored with a freshly ground rasam powder that includes toor dal for body and thickness. Distinctive for its raw-extraction technique — tomatoes and tamarind are ground and strained cold, preserving fresh flavor without boiling.
